messages:
Maya (CS): Heads-up: creating a 1-paragraph customer runbook named 'Surge Shield' for go-lives. Needs concrete 3-step actions: readiness, instant fallbacks, and 24h feedback that maps to renewal signals.

Omar (SRE): Keep it action-first. My 3 recovery knobs: toggle streaming, raise cache TTL, lower batch size. Add thresholds.

Tess (PM): Include a pasteable JSON snippet and one-line CRM rule: if customer flags latency or quality at 24h, set renewal_risk=true.

Maya (CS): Draft copy (paste to customer):
"Surge Shield — 3-minute runbook"
1) Readiness: pin model, enable prefix cache (TTL=600s), set batching target=12, streaming=on.
2) Instant fallbacks: if 95p latency >200ms -> (a) increase cache TTL to 1200s; (b) disable streaming for route; (c) reduce target_batch_size to 6. If errors >1% for 5m, switch to fallback_model=redwood-lite-v1 and notify support.
3) 24h feedback: "Any latency spikes or quality issues? Reply yes/no + route + sample input." If No in either latency or quality, CS will recommend dedicated capacity.

Jordan (Customer): Useful. Can you add one-line when to prefill vs TTL?

Maya (CS): "Use higher TTL for repeat prompts across sessions; add prefill entries for short deterministic fragments at session start"

ops-bot: runbook 'surge-shield' created at 3618000055 by Maya (CS).
